room_or_space: Fireplace elevations (East and West faces) of one chimney mass serving three vertically stacked levels; the rooms are not named on the sheet

overall_dimensions.ceiling_height: 7'-6" (top tier), 7'-3" (middle tier), 7'-2" (lowest tier), all on the East elevation; a 1'-5" floor zone separates the top and middle tiers

proportions.notable_proportion: Three stacked tiers of near-equal, low floor-to-ceiling height (7'-2" to 7'-6"); fireplace openings, hearth shelves and lintel bands are drawn as wide, low horizontals, markedly wider than they are high; brick coursing is drawn as continuous horizontal lines reinforcing the horizontal emphasis

layout.organisation: Two elevations side by side (labelled EAST, left, and WEST, right) of the same chimney mass, each in three vertically stacked tiers separated by floor/ceiling lines. Top tier: on the East a hipped-roof outline and chimney cap above a continuous band of framed stippled panels; on the West the plain brick chimney shaft with a sloping roof edge and a column of small rectangular recesses. Middle tier: brick fireplace with a wide low opening, raised hearth plinth and a rectangular void through the brick above the shelf. Lowest tier: brick fireplace with a wide opening, raised hearth blocks and a long projecting shelf slab, flanked on the West by tall framed stippled piers.
layout.axes: A single vertical stacking axis through the chimney. The West elevation fireplaces are roughly symmetrical about a vertical centreline; the East elevation is asymmetric, with stepped stair profiles and a sectioned post to the left and right of the fireplaces.
layout.entry_sequence: Not shown; the sheet contains elevations only, with no doors into the spaces indicated.
layout.circulation: Heavy sectioned stepped profiles (with dashed hidden steps) beside the East-elevation fireplaces show a stair descending next to the chimney mass between the middle and lowest tiers; no other circulation is shown.
